slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
If the Loire is the kingdom of Cabernet Franc, then Chinon, Bourgueil, and Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil are its triple-peaked crown. This lesson explores how the same grape variety expresses itself differently across different soils — from the structured tuffeau plateau of Chinon to the lighter gravel terraces of Saint-Nicolas — and why these wines are among France's most food-friendly reds.

AOCs Covered in This Lesson

Chinon, Bourgueil, Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil
slides.1.title: Chinon — The Soul of Cabernet Franc
slides.1.content:
🏰 Chinon

Centered on the medieval fortress town of Chinon in Indre-et-Loire, this is the Loire's most celebrated red appellation. Three distinct soil types produce three distinct styles:

  • Tuffeau plateaux: Structured, age-worthy wines with mineral depth — best expressions last 10–20 years
  • Gravel terraces: Supple, fresh, red-fruit focused — best enjoyed young at 12–14°C
  • Sandy clay: Light, easy-drinking, early-harvest style

Typical aromatics: raspberry, red currant, violet, pencil shavings, subtle earthy minerality.

🌿 Bourgueil and Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil

Bourgueil: On the north bank of the Loire between Tours and Saumur. Tuffeau plateau wines are structured and can age; gravel wines are fresh and approachable.

Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil: A separate AOC entirely on gravel soils — lighter, more immediately charming, excellent at 13°C with charcuterie.

Key difference: Saint-Nicolas is 100% gravel → always lighter and earlier-drinking than Bourgueil's tuffeau cuvées.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which AOC is covered in this lesson?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Chinon is one of the Loire's most important red wine AOCs — the heartland of Cabernet Franc. Its tuffeau and gravel soils create two distinct styles: structured age-worthy reds from the plateau and lighter, fresher wines from the gravel terraces.
